posts.title: What goes in the kitchen before you land
posts.excerpt: Before Kwame brings you across the bay from Port Avel, Priya Nair stocks your villa kitchen with fresh provisions and your first morning breakfast.
posts.content:
Every stay booked directly with us begins well before your boat leaves the slipway in Port Avel. Seven days prior to your arrival date, Rosa Delgado writes to confirm which boat you plan to take—the 10:00, 13:00, or 16:00 crossing—and to ask for your household grocery list. We do not stock standardized snack hampers or packaged minibar items. Instead, Priya Nair takes your notes, visits local producers in town, and brings everything across to Lune Cay on Captain Kwame’s morning run.

By the time you step ashore at the jetty, your kitchen is fully prepared. In each of our nine houses—whether you are staying in a Reef House by the water’s edge, a Lagoon House above the shallows, or one of the Hill Houses overlooking the north point—the timber counters are set with fresh supplies. Priya arranges fresh bread, seasonal fruit such as mangoes and limes, farm eggs, and fresh ground coffee for your first morning. There is fresh milk in the larder, olive oil, sea salt, and any specific provisions you requested during the week leading up to your arrival.

This personalized approach allows us to care for every guest thoughtfully. In August 2026, when the Adeyemi family of five arrived to stay at Hill House, Priya planned and sourced every ingredient around a detailed nut-allergy list they had sent the week before. Having our own kitchen team means guests with dietary preferences or young children can settle in immediately without worrying about shopping after a day of travel. You unlock your door at 14:00, unpack your bags, and find everything you need to brew a hot drink or prepare a light meal overlooking the sea.

Throughout your stay, Priya is also available to cook dinner in your villa. For €140 per evening, she or a member of her kitchen team prepares a complete evening meal for up to six guests directly in your kitchen. Many guests like to spend late afternoons swimming off the reef steps or resting by the plunge pool, knowing that dinner is being prepared on the terrace. Afterward, she clears the counters and leaves dessert, leaving you to enjoy the evening breeze and the sound of the water under the lanterns.

Each morning follows a calm island rhythm. At 07:40, Rosa walks along the shaded sand paths to deliver warm bread to the houses before the heat rises. Jonas Weber tends the garden beds and plunge pools, while Mei Lin Tan opens the guest desk at The Jetty House from 08:00 to 20:00 to answer questions or arrange extra supplies. If you need additional items during your stay, Kwame can easily bring them over from Port Avel on his 13:00 boat.

We have run Shimaya Villas this way since Ana and Theo founded the houses in 2011. Because we sell every night ourselves without booking platforms, the people you communicate with before you arrive are the very people preparing your home on the island. When your departure day comes, direct guests keep their house until 16:00, enjoying a final swim and a relaxed lunch before walking down to Kwame’s 16:15 boat back to Port Avel.

posts.title: The 10:00 boat from Port Avel
posts.excerpt: Kwame’s crossing from Port Avel to Lune Cay: what to expect.
posts.content:
Kwame Mensah runs three boats a day in season: from Port Avel at 10:00, 13:00 and 16:00, and back from Lune Cay at 09:15, 12:15 and 16:15. The crossing takes 40 minutes and the boat is included in every stay.

When Henrik travelled with his parents in October 2025, Kwame put a chair at the boat’s step for his father. Tell us who is coming and we will do the same for you.

The reef shows through the water as you come in. That is when most guests put their phones away.

posts.title: Why we close the houses in November
posts.excerpt: Why the houses are closed from November to March, and what happens while they are.
posts.content:
The houses are open from 1 April to 31 October and closed from November to March. The reef rests, Theo repairs the timber, Jonas rebuilds the paths and the whole island team is paid through the winter.

That is one reason we let every night ourselves. With no commission to pay, the closed months are paid for, and the same people are back in April to open the doors.

Dates for the next season open in January. A 30% deposit confirms a hold, and the balance is due 30 days before arrival.
